data.body: Root cause confirmed and fix implemented. RCA: reducer/_cache.py prepare_event_files sets cache_path = <ticket_dir>/.cache.json and write_cache (the single publish seam, called from reducer/_api.py and reducer/_processors.py) atomic_write's it INSIDE the snapshot entry whenever the tracker root is a pinned snapshot (store layout <base>/rebar-gate-snapshots/tickets-<40hex>/.tickets-tracker/<id>). ADR 0005 D2 documents entries as immutable post-publish; hardlink blob-sharing (b7a4994742) raises the stakes for any in-place write. Fix (least-behavioral option, sanctioned by ticket text 'e.g. the reducer cache is disabled...when the tracker root is a snapshot'): new structural predicate in_snapshot_entry() in _snapshot/repo_snapshot.py (consecutive path parts: rebar-gate-snapshots / (tickets-)?[0-9a-f]{40}), and write_cache no-ops when ticket_dir is inside an entry — the cache is a rebuildable optimization, so pinned-root reads simply stay uncached. AC3 pinned: new test asserts fsutil.atomic_write publishes via rename (os.replace), never in-place. AC4: ADR 0005 D2 amended to state reader-side immutability and the two guards. Tests: tests/unit/test_snapshot_entry_immutability_5c27.py (RED observed first: .cache.json appeared in entry after a read; predicate absent). All green: targeted suites 67 passed, reducer/cache -k 193 passed, make lint, make typecheck, complexity new=0 increased=0.
